mainTopic: רבי אליעזר's view on impurity late in a נזירות term, and the מחלוקת of רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש about a נזירות vow made in a cemetery.
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining the earlier משנה. רבי אליעזר holds that impurity after a נזירות term is complete cancels only seven days. He agrees that everything is cancelled when someone explicitly vowed thirty full days. The hundred-day case is sent back to the earlier discussion of בר פדא and רב מתנא. Then a new משנה teaches that someone who vows נזירות inside a בית הקברות does not count those days and brings no impurity offering. If he leaves and re-enters, he does count the days and does bring the offering, unless, says רבי אליעזר, he re-enters on the same day. In the גמרא, רבי יוחנן says such a vow takes effect and waits until he is pure, while ריש לקיש says it does not take effect at all. ריש לקיש deflects רבי יוחנן's first challenge from the משנה. רבי יוחנן then brings a ברייתא that gives מלקות to a טמא person who vowed, and the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: The reasoning behind רבי אליעזר's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that רבי אליעזר holds that impurity after the term is complete cancels only seven days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר holds: any impurity that happens after the term is complete cancels only seven days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason for רבי אליעזר's opinion in the משנה. Once the נזירות term is finished, becoming impure only cancels seven days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר treats impurity after completion (מלאת) as a separate, smaller problem from impurity during the term. Impurity during the term wipes out everything, but impurity after completion cancels only seven days. In the earlier משנה's case of a plain נזירות vow, he treats day thirty as already after completion, so impurity on that day cancels only seven.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer holds:
Any impurity after completion cancels only seven.
phrases.notes: He means seven days: just the impurity period, not the whole נזירות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the explanation of רבי אליעזר's view from the earlier משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי אליעזר, impurity after the term is complete cancels only seven days.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר agrees when 'thirty full days' were vowed
steps.stepSummary: In the case of 'I am a נזיר for thirty days' with impurity on day thirty, everything is cancelled, and רבי אליעזר agrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone said 'I am a נזיר for thirty days' and became impure on the thirtieth day, it cancels everything. רבי אליעזר does not argue here, because he said full days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another line of the משנה and explains why רבי אליעזר does not argue with it. The person explicitly said thirty days, so the whole thirtieth day is part of his term.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 limited cancellation to seven days only for impurity after completion. Here the person said 'thirty days' outright, which means thirty complete days. So day thirty is still inside the term, not after it. Impurity during the term cancels everything, even for רבי אליעזר.

keyTerms.meaning: I am hereby a נזיר (the vow formula)

steps.confusionAlert: This does not contradict step 1. Seven days is רבי אליעזר's rule only when the impurity comes after the term is complete. Here day thirty is still inside the term.

phrases.english: "I am hereby a nazirite for thirty days,"

phrases.aramaic: וְנִטְמָא יוֹם שְׁלֹשִׁים — סוֹתֵר אֶת הַכֹּל,
phrases.english: and he became impure on day thirty: it cancels everything.
Rabbi Eliezer does not disagree,
since he said full days.
phrases.notes: He explicitly said 'thirty days,' so all of day thirty is part of the vow.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא פְּלִיג רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר דְּאָמַר שְׁלֵימִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets a limit on step 1's principle: an explicit vow of thirty days keeps day thirty inside the term.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When thirty days were explicitly vowed, impurity on day thirty cancels everything, even according to רבי אליעזר.

steps.title: The hundred-day case follows the earlier discussion
steps.stepSummary: For 'a נזיר for a hundred days' with impurity on day one hundred, the גמרא refers back to the views of בר פדא and רב מתנא.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'I am a נזיר for a hundred days,' and he became impure on day one hundred: it cancels everything. רבי אליעזר says it cancels only thirty. This whole case is explained as we discussed it earlier, following בר פדא and רב מתנא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the hundred-day case from the משנה. It does not explain it again. It says to understand it the way it was already discussed earlier with בר פדא and רב מתנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the חכמים say everything is cancelled, but רבי אליעזר says only thirty days are lost. Instead of repeating the analysis, the גמרא sends us back to the earlier סוגיא that dealt with these exact opinions. That closes the discussion of this משנה.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אליעזר's rule: impurity after the term is complete cancels less, only seven days. He agrees that impurity inside an explicitly vowed term cancels everything. The hundred-day case was already worked out with בר פדא and רב מתנא.

phrases.english: "I am hereby a nazirite for one hundred days,"

phrases.aramaic: וְנִטְמָא יוֹם מֵאָה — סוֹתֵר אֶת הַכֹּל,
phrases.english: and he became impure on day one hundred: it cancels everything.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: אֵינוֹ סוֹתֵר אֶלָּא שְׁלֹשִׁים.
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: it cancels only thirty.
And all of it is as we discussed it,
according to bar Padda and Rav Mattana.
phrases.notes: This points back to the earlier discussion on דף ה and ו.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכוּלָּהּ כְּדַהֲוֵינַן בָּהּ אַלִּיבָּא דְּבַר פַּדָּא וְרַב מַתְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes going through the משנה's cases by sending the last one back to an earlier discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The hundred-day case is explained by the earlier analysis of בר פדא and רב מתנא.

steps.title: A vow of נזירות made inside a cemetery
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה: a vow made inside a בית הקברות does not start counting until he leaves. If he leaves and re-enters, the days count and he brings impurity offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who vowed נזירות while in a cemetery, even if he stayed there thirty days, those days do not count toward his total, and he does not bring an impurity offering. If he left and then came back in, the days do count and he brings an impurity offering.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that a נזירות vow made while already impure in a cemetery does not start counting until he leaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While he stays in the cemetery, his days are not counted, so there are no pure נזירות days to lose. That is why he brings no impurity offering. Once he leaves, his נזירות can begin. Going back in is then a real breach, so the days count and he brings the impurity offering.

keyTerms.meaning: The impurity offering(s) of a נזיר

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who vowed naziriteship while he was in a cemetery,
even if he was there thirty days,
they do not count toward his tally,
and he does not bring an offering of impurity.
If he left and then entered again,
they do count toward his tally,
and he brings an offering of impurity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Days in the cemetery after the vow do not count and bring no offering. After leaving and re-entering, the days count and he brings an impurity offering.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: not if he re-enters the same day
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר says that re-entering on the very day he left does not bring the offering, because he needs 'first days' of pure נזירות first.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: not on that same day, as it says 'and the first days shall fall away.' He needs to have first days.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר limits the end of the משנה. If he goes back into the cemetery on the same day he left, he does not bring the impurity offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר learns from the words 'the first days shall fall away' that a נזיר brings impurity offerings only if he has some earlier pure days to lose. Someone who re-enters on the same day he left has no 'first days' yet. So for him the rule of the משנה does not apply.
steps.whatToRemember: A נזיר brings impurity offerings only when he has pure נזירות days to lose. According to רבי אליעזר, re-entering the cemetery on the same day he left does not count.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: לֹא בּוֹ בַיּוֹם,
phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says: not on that very day,
as it is stated: "And the first days shall fall away,"
until he will have first days.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: לֹא בּוֹ בַיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the last ruling of step 4 (leaving and re-entering) for the case of re-entering on the same day.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Re-entering on the same day he left brings no impurity offering, because he needs earlier pure days first.

steps.title: A vow made in a cemetery: does it take effect?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says נזירות takes effect on one who vows in a בית הקברות. ריש לקיש says it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: It was stated: if someone vowed to be a נזיר while he was in a cemetery, רבי יוחנן said the נזירות takes effect on him, and ריש לקיש said it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of the משנה with a מחלוקת between two אמוראים about a person who makes a vow of נזירות while standing in a בית הקברות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה already said his days do not count until he leaves. The new question is more basic: is he a נזיר at all right now? רבי יוחנן says yes, and ריש לקיש says no.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated. This opens a מחלוקת of אמוראים.
A cemetery, a place full of טומאת מת.

phrases.english: GEMARA: It was stated:
one who vowed to be a nazir while he was in a cemetery,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: נְזִירוּת חָלָה עָלָיו,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said: nazirus takes effect on him,

phrases.aramaic: וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: אֵין נְזִירוּת חָלָה עָלָיו.
phrases.english: and Reish Lakish said: nazirus does not take effect on him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיתְּמַר, מִי שֶׁנָּזַר וְהוּא בְּבֵית הַקְּבָרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the new משנה from step 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: נזירות takes effect. ריש לקיש: it does not.

steps.title: Explaining each side's reasoning
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן holds that the vow is on hold and kicks in once he is pure. ריש לקיש holds that it never took hold, so he must vow again after leaving.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן, who said נזירות takes effect, holds that it hangs and waits, and once it finds purity it takes effect. ריש לקיש, who said it does not take effect, holds that if he says the vow again it takes effect, and if not, it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what each אמורא means and what the practical difference is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן the vow is already real but on hold; when he leaves and becomes pure, it starts by itself. For ריש לקיש the vow made in the cemetery is empty. He becomes a נזיר only if he vows again outside.

keyTerms.meaning: It hangs and stands waiting, meaning it is on hold.
He said it again, meaning he repeated the vow.

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides agree he does not start counting days while he is in the cemetery. Their argument is whether his first vow is already binding, or whether he must vow again after leaving.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר נְזִירוּת חָלָה עָלָיו, סָבַר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan, who said nazirus takes effect on him, holds:
it hangs and stands waiting,
once it finds purity, it takes effect.

phrases.aramaic: וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: אֵין נְזִירוּת חָלָה עָלָיו.
phrases.english: And Reish Lakish said: nazirus does not take effect on him.
If he says it again, it takes effect on him,
phrases.notes: He means after he has left the cemetery.

phrases.english: and if not, then not.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר נְזִירוּת חָלָה עָלָיו, סָבַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning and practical difference of the מחלוקת in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: the vow is on hold until purity. ריש לקיש: the vow is void and must be repeated.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's challenge from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says only that he does not bring a קרבן טומאה. That suggests the נזירות itself does take effect, against ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן challenged ריש לקיש from the משנה: one who vowed in a cemetery, even if he was there thirty days, those days do not count, and he does not bring a קרבן טומאה. So it is only the קרבן טומאה that he does not bring, but the נזירות does take effect!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן quotes our משנה and reads it closely to attack ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists only two things he lacks: the days do not count, and there is no קרבן טומאה. It does not say he is not a נזיר. רבי יוחנן reads this to mean the נזירות itself is in place.

keyTerms.meaning: He challenged him from a source.
They do not count toward the total of days.
The offering a נזיר brings when he becomes טמא.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan challenged Reish Lakish:
One who vowed nazirus while in a cemetery,
even if he was there thirty days,
they do not count toward the tally,
and he does not bring an offering of impurity.
It is the offering of impurity that he does not bring,
but as for taking effect, it does take effect on him!
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוחנן's own inference: since the משנה leaves the נזירות out of its list, the נזירות must be in place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks ריש לקיש's view from step 7 using the משנה from step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that נזירות does not take effect in a בית הקברות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה denies him only the counting of days and the קרבן טומאה. This implies the נזירות itself takes effect.

steps.title: ריש לקיש: no טומאה rules, so no קרבן
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש reads the משנה differently: he is not under the rules of טומאה at all, so of course there is no קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said to him: he is not under the law of טומאה, and so he is not under the law of the קרבן.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש answers by rereading the משנה's words about the קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן read the line about the קרבן as the only thing missing. ריש לקיש says it shows the opposite: there is no קרבן because he is not a נזיר at all, so the rules of נזיר טומאה do not apply to him.

keyTerms.meaning: Under the law or category of.

phrases.english: He said to him: he is not under the law of impurity,
and he is not under the law of the offering.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה denies only the קרבן, so the נזירות is in place.
steps.terutzMaskana: No קרבן because he is not a נזיר at all, so the rules of נזיר טומאה do not apply to him.

steps.title: Second challenge: why does he get מלקות?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says one who was טמא and vowed gets forty lashes if he shaves, drinks wine, or becomes טמא. That only makes sense if the נזירות took effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: He challenged him again: one who was טמא and vowed נזירות is forbidden to shave, drink wine, or become טמא to the dead, and if he did, he gets the forty lashes. If you say the נזירות takes effect, that is why he gets lashes. But if you say it does not take effect, why does he get lashes?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן brings a second, stronger challenge from a ברייתא about a טמא person who vowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מלקות are given only for breaking a real איסור. If a טמא person who vows gets מלקות for breaking נזיר rules, then his נזירות must already be in force even while he is טמא. That contradicts ריש לקיש. The answer comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: He receives the forty lashes, which is מלקות.

phrases.english: He challenged him: one who was impure and vowed nazirus,
is forbidden to shave and to drink wine
and to become impure from the dead.
And if he shaved or drank wine
or became impure from the dead,
he receives the forty lashes.
Granted, if you say it takes effect,
that is the reason he receives the forty lashes,
but if you say it does not take effect,
why does he receive the forty lashes?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After ריש לקיש deflected the first challenge, רבי יוחנן brings a second source.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that נזירות does not take effect on someone who is טמא when he vows.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מלקות require a real איסור. Lashes for breaking נזיר rules prove the נזירות took effect while he was טמא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This challenge uses מלקות, a concrete penalty, so it is harder to explain away than the first challenge about the קרבן.
